text: One truck and one equipment job. One truck covers the assigned area and handles one job at a time. Send it to the pole or other electrical equipment that needs inspection or repair. Check crew and route safety first, then flood clearance for the proposed work. Rank eligible jobs by highest affected customer tier, most customers expected to regain power, most linked outage reports, and shortest driving ETA. Recheck the highest tier after each job and when conditions change.

metadata.title: One truck and one equipment job

text: Safety is the first dispatch check. Each proposed pole job is marked Safe or Unsafe based on the crew's ability to safely reach and perform the proposed work. Debris, blocked access, or flooding at the work site or along the route can make a job unsafe. Hold unsafe jobs regardless of customer tier or restoration scope. Reassess held jobs when conditions change.

metadata.title: Safety is the first dispatch check

text: Flood clearance determines what work can proceed. Check flood clearance after crew and route safety, before ranking jobs. Clear means the facility has no flood restriction in this fixture. Flooded, partial cleared means authorized personnel have verified that a specified unaffected section can safely receive power separately. Limit restoration to that approved scope. At a multi-floor hospital, approved upper floors may be served while flood-affected areas remain on hold. A dry floor alone does not establish clearance. Flooded, hold means restoration waits for clearance. An independently cleared inspection can still be dispatched as an inspection-only job. Flood status affects eligible work and scope. Rank eligible jobs using the normal factors.

metadata.title: Flood clearance determines what work can proceed

text: Three customer priority tiers. Level 1 is Critical: hospitals, including multi-floor hospitals, evacuation centers, and schools currently serving as evacuation centers. Level 2 is Community services: schools in regular use, barangay halls, and public markets. Level 3 is Residential: houses and apartments. Use the highest affected tier served by the equipment. For example, a pole serving an affected hospital and affected homes is one Level 1 job. Move down only when there is no eligible pending job in a higher tier.

Expected restoration customer count. Among eligible jobs in the same tier, prioritize the repair expected to restore electricity to more affected customers. Count the affected customers expected to regain power within the approved restoration scope. A multi-floor hospital with one service connection counts as one customer even when several floors are approved for partial restoration. Include any homes or other customers restored by the same repair. Outage reports are recorded separately from customer count.

Reports break equal customer counts. If two safe jobs have the same tier and the same expected number of customers restored, prioritize the job with more linked outage reports. Apply report count after tier and customer count.

Shorter driving ETA breaks the remaining tie. If two safe jobs tie on tier, expected customers restored, and report count, choose the shorter Google Maps driving ETA from the current truck location to the equipment. A farther pole can have a shorter ETA. Use safety status to decide whether a route and work site are eligible.

metadata.title: Shorter driving ETA breaks the remaining tie

text: Synthetic demo case case-01: Safety first. The hospital pole is unsafe and the evacuation center pole is safe. Expected action: DISPATCH to P-EVAC. Send the truck to the evacuation center pole and hold the hospital pole job.

Synthetic demo case case-02: Critical before residential. Both poles are safe. The hospital pole has 2 reports and a 15-minute ETA. The residential pole serves 80 homes, has 30 reports, and has a 4-minute ETA. Expected action: DISPATCH to P-HOSP. Send the truck to the hospital pole. The critical tier takes priority over residential jobs.

Synthetic demo case case-03: More customers restored. Both poles are safe and critical. The hospital pole restores the hospital and 40 homes. The evacuation center pole restores the center and 10 homes and has more reports. Expected action: DISPATCH to P-HOSP. Send the truck to the hospital pole. The repair is expected to restore 41 customers versus 11.

Synthetic demo case case-04: Reports break the tie. There are no pending critical jobs. The safe school and barangay hall pole jobs each restore 20 customers. The school has 4 reports and a 6-minute ETA. The barangay hall has 9 reports and a 12-minute ETA. Expected action: DISPATCH to P-HALL. Send the truck to the barangay hall pole. The jobs tie on tier and restoration customer count, so reports decide.

Synthetic demo case case-05: Farther pole is faster. The two safe critical pole jobs tie on customer count and reports. The hospital pole is 1 km away with an 18-minute ETA. The evacuation center pole is 2 km away with an 8-minute ETA. Expected action: DISPATCH to P-EVAC. Send the truck to the evacuation center pole. Its driving ETA is shorter.

Synthetic demo case case-06: Move down to Level 2. The hospital and evacuation center poles are unsafe. The school and residential poles are both safe. Expected action: DISPATCH to P-SCHOOL. Send the truck to the school pole. Level 2 is the highest tier with a safe pending job.

Synthetic demo case case-07: Move down to Level 3. Critical work is completed and community service jobs are unsafe and on hold. Two safe residential pole jobs would restore 12 homes and 5 homes, respectively. Expected action: DISPATCH to P-HOMES-A. Send the truck to the pole serving 12 homes. Level 3 is the highest available tier and this repair restores more customers.
Synthetic demo case case-08: No safe jobs. All pending pole jobs are unsafe. Expected action: HOLD. Hold the truck and check the queue again when a job is marked safe.

Synthetic demo case case-09: School serving as an evacuation center. Both school pole jobs are safe. School A is serving as an evacuation center. School B is in regular use and has a shorter ETA, more reports, and more customers affected. Expected action: DISPATCH to P-SHELTER-SCHOOL. Send the truck to School A's pole. A school serving as an evacuation center is Level 1, and a school in regular use is Level 2.

metadata.title: School serving as an evacuation center

text: Synthetic demo case case-10: Multi-floor hospital cleared for partial restoration. The hospital ground floor is flooded. The route and pole work are safe. Authorized personnel have cleared floors 2 to 4 for separate restoration. The evacuation center pole is also safe. Both jobs serve one customer connection and have three reports. The hospital ETA is seven minutes and the evacuation center ETA is twelve minutes. Expected action: DISPATCH to P-HOSP. Send the truck to the hospital pole for the approved partial restoration. The jobs tie on tier, customer count, and reports, so the shorter hospital ETA wins. Floors 2 to 4 are cleared and the ground floor is held.

metadata.title: Multi-floor hospital cleared for partial restoration

text: Synthetic demo case case-11: Hospital restoration on flood hold. The hospital pole is safely accessible, but restoration to the flooded hospital has no clearance. The pending hospital job is restoration. An evacuation center pole is safe and ready for restoration. Expected action: DISPATCH to P-EVAC. Hold the hospital restoration and send the truck to the evacuation center pole.

Synthetic demo case case-12: Crew safety blocks partial restoration. The hospital has partial restoration clearance for the upper floors, but the route to its pole is unsafe. An evacuation center pole has a safe route and safe work conditions. Expected action: DISPATCH to P-EVAC. Hold the hospital job because the crew cannot safely reach its pole. Send the truck to the evacuation center pole.

Synthetic demo case case-13: Safe inspection while restoration is held. The hospital has a pending, cleared pole inspection. The inspection can be performed safely. Restoration to the flooded hospital is on hold. Expected action: DISPATCH to P-HOSP. Send the truck to inspect the hospital pole only. Keep restoration on hold pending clearance.

metadata.title: Safe inspection while restoration is held
